title: Staff are not told they are talking to an AI system: the chat page never says so (EU AI Act Article 50, in force since 2 August 2026)
controls: Add a visible AI notice to the chat page and to the /ask response
Classification and obligations written down in governance/capstone_classification.md

title: Nobody regularly reads the questions the chatbot declines or blocks, so wrong or missing answers go unnoticed
controls: Dashboard with alert rules for decline rate, errors and cost
Runbook says who looks at the alerts

title: A question or a planted document contains instructions that change the chatbot's answers (prompt injection)
controls: Red-team attacks run before each release: 1 of 5 worked before the guardrails, 0 of 5 after

title: An agent tool changes or reassigns a help desk ticket wrongly, or a role is given tools it should not have
controls: Role permissions: each agent may only use the tools listed for it
update_ticket needs a person to approve each call

title: The chatbot gives a wrong or uncited answer and staff act on it
controls: Quality gate with agreed thresholds, run before each release
Every answer must cite its source; checks reject answers without one

title: Routing simple questions to the small model makes answers worse (it failed the quality gate: wrong P1 response time)
controls: Routing is off by default (ROUTING=1 is needed to turn it on)
Routing only goes live if the quality gate passes with it on

title: The model provider is down or slow and staff get no answers
controls: Runbook for the person on call

title: Personal data from a question or a document shows up in an answer or a log
controls: Personal data is redacted from questions and answers (Presidio)
Only request metadata is logged, not the question text

title: Heavy use or an agent that keeps calling tools runs up the model bill
controls: Response cache, and cost reported per month
reason: The cost report puts the bill at about $62 a month for 10,000 questions a day, and the 6-step limit stops loops. Worst case is a few cents per question, which is small for an internal tool.
